newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - September 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - September 11.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

MEXICO CITY - The Walt Disney Co is poised to sign its first-ever pay-TV distribution deal south of the border -- with top Latino programmer HBO Ole, a joint venture between Time Warner, Sony Corp and Venezuelan investors.

HOLLYWOOD - Arnold Rifkin, the worldwide president of the motion picture group at the William Morris Agency, has been offered the job of chairman of Sony's Columbia-TriStar Motion Picture Companies, now held by Mark Canton, and has entered into negotiations with the company.
HOLLYWOOD - HBO captured 111 nominations in voting for the 18th Annual CableACE Awards, matching the combined total of its six closest competitors.
TORONTO - No major new movies have been forthcoming at the 21st Toronto International Film Festival, but there has been no shortage of good, reasonably engaging films.
HOLLYWOOD - ABC Entertainment senior vice president Michael Rosenfeld has resigned after less than one year in the job.
